$comment: Signal K server settings for lcars-helm. Placeholders are replaced by deploy/provision.sh on the Pi and by scripts/setup-dev-signalk.mjs during development. The two differ only in the host names, so what runs on the bench is what runs on the boat. The connection is UDP because that is what Cinderella's actual YDWG-02 is configured for: RAW protocol on UDP 1457, bidirectional; TCP 1456 on this gateway carries NMEA 0183 (transmit-only), a different and older protocol that is not what this connects to. Confirmed against the real gateway on 2026-08-14 — canboatjs decoded 41 distinct PGNs from a 15-second capture, including rudder, heading, wind, rate of turn, GPS and speed.

subOptions.$comment: `host` is only used if Signal K ever writes back to the gateway; it plays no part in receiving. The UDP provider binds `port` locally and accepts any datagram that arrives there — a broadcast socket, not a connection — which is also why there is nothing here like the TCP provider's noDataReceivedTimeout: there is no socket to go stale after a WiFi blip. Signal K just keeps listening, and picks back up the moment packets resume.
